dimensions.abu-saraj-iv17: Plan 5 scale, 3 m / 178 sampled pixels. Uniform height 1.55 m within reported 1.4–1.7 m. Roof cap, rock thickness, masonry height and scan sampling illustrative.
dimensions.hyrcania-waterworks: Northern pool floor at -5 m, southern member at -2.6 m; approximate published northern sides. Rock separation 5.1 m within reported 4.8–5.4 m. Southern footprint, bridge, summit and other cistern dimensions illustrative.
dimensions.gerizim-precinct: Reported 212 × 136 m enclosure, 40 × 40 m mansion, 20 × 14 m building IV, 25 × 24 m citadel. East stair uses maximum 23 m width, 34 m run, 15.5 m rise and approximately 57 steps. Western landing distinct from southern seven-step and E1 flights. Other heights, divisions, cistern and platform relief illustrative.
dimensions.jericho-early: Approximate 18 × 13 m pool envelopes; 2.5 m depth, columns and platform illustrative.
dimensions.jericho-late: Approximate 32 × 18 m joined envelope; 2.5 m depth, columns and platform illustrative.
dimensions.relative_models: Doq, Qumran, Siloam and Area AC are normalized relative frames. Heights/depths and channel cross-sections illustrative; selection envelopes are not measured footprints.

landscape.method: Modern elevation sampled around existing site anchors, with a feathered display bench and source-qualified architectural volumes. Terrain is contextual; footprint placement and compass bearing are illustrative. IV/17 uses an illustrative setting without coordinates.

surface_art.method: Original deterministic 512-pixel colour and relief/roughness tiles, projected in world metres. Separate masonry, limestone, stratified bedrock, soil and plaster treatments. Physical chipped stone courses, coping, open channel troughs, grounded rubble and sparse vegetation; no publication or photograph pixels are used as texture maps. Dominant-axis projection preserves hard surface detail; soil combines two differently oriented samples to reduce visible tiling.

profiles.Qumran: Warm fractured limestone and dusty ground; uneven crest, tapering rock beds, short weathered ledges and an angular recess. An irregular feathered ground apron replaces the rectangular tile.
profiles.Doq: Ochre limestone and rough desert masonry around the plan-derived cistern/channel relations.
profiles.Hyrcania: Cream limestone and muted plaster distinguish the paired basins.
profiles.Jericho: Warm stone, reddish soil and pale worn plaster; source states remain separate.
profiles.Gerizim: Cooler ashlar palette and sparse sage vegetation around the precinct/stair relationships.
profiles.Siloam: Grey-gold limestone and muted plaster around the small receiving-basin tracing.

surface_art.evidence_limit: Palette, chipping, individual stone joints, cliff bedding, plaster wear, rubble, vegetation, light and sky are illustrative surface art. These additions supply no new archaeological observations, dimensions, phase assignments or identification evidence.
surface_art.rendering: Directional sun, hemisphere fill, ACES tone mapping, static shadow map, eye-level sky; 2048-pixel desktop / 1024-pixel phone shadow atlas. Repeated masonry and scree use GPU instancing. Thin soil floors receive shadows without casting self-shadow artifacts. Regional source layers pause at eye level and regain their individual visibility on exit; the site and sky continue rendering in the same geographic canvas.
surface_art.camera: Initial eye-level positions frame a source feature such as the eastern stair, pool rim or channel. These are display viewpoints, not surveyed camera positions or walking routes. Eye-level look can pass above the horizon to inspect cliff faces and tall structures; exiting restores the normal geographic camera limits. The first-person camera now follows a physical capsule body, with gravity and clearance against the displayed geometry; a 65-degree field of view reveals the original block-style body.
surface_art.covered_passages: The normalized Reeder–Jol scene uses angular rock-cut display sections in place of smooth tubes. Their rectangular roof section is illustrative. A copper-coloured lining retains the proposed-course distinction in the source.

unified_map.renderer: MapLibre shared geographic WebGL canvas with a Three.js custom layer. Source-based 3D appears on close zoom; eye-level inspection uses the same camera and canvas.
unified_map.placement: Existing site anchors only. Architectural bearing, local origin, relative display scale and alignment remain illustrative; this interface does not register the source plans to the earth.
unified_map.qumran: Detailed aqueduct segment reuses the existing Ilan–Amit 1989 p. 283 Fig. 1 relationships and existing Davey CJD979 comparison. Rock faces, masonry weathering, cross-sections and heights are illustrative; the whole settlement is not reconstructed.
unified_map.walking: Embodied first-person character: 1.8 m high, 0.28 m capsule radius, standing eye 1.65 m, crouching height 1.2 m and eye 1.05 m. Fixed 120 Hz physics applies gravity, jumping, wall sliding, 0.35 m steps, a 50-degree slope limit and head clearance. Ground, rock, walls and ceilings collide; repeated masonry uses oriented bounding boxes, small pebbles and vegetation are excluded. Qumran collision geometry rebuilds after the loaded map terrain deforms it. Visible block-style sleeves, hands, legs and boots follow the character. Walking speed is 3.4 m/s and sprint speed 5.6 m/s. These collision/display approximations do not establish a surveyed ancient walking route.
unified_map.photos: Original licensed source JPEGs are archived with provenance at research/assets/plans/atlas-ground-photographs; matching atlas mirror and public copies retain identical bytes, authors and license links.
unified_map.videos: The two existing Qumran YouTube leads are labeled unreviewed. They are inline reference players, not inspected geometry input or registered camera tracks. User-entered links store video IDs locally in the browser.
unified_map.access: No fresh private Google Drive file retrieval or live YouTube playback verification is claimed. Inline Drive preview uses the viewer account permissions; provider domains are saved in the environment draft.
unified_map.validation: The exact actions/jekyll-build-pages image generated an 88.8 MiB site. Every app file retains its source bytes, startup assets resolve and the research archives are excluded. Chromium checks against that actual Pages output passed on desktop and phone: rendered source geometry, persistent map canvas, inline plan/photo/Drive/video references, eye-level movement, looking above the horizon, return to map, site switching and unavailable-provider messages. A controlled Terrarium DEM at -183 metres verifies that loaded elevation and the rendered model stay in view through Terrain/Map switching. Desktop and phone renders using the existing archived Wadi Qumran Mapterhorn patch were inspected in overview and at eye level: no rectangular soil tile or transparent cut-out edges; soil, rock, scree and channels follow the same slope. The shared ground fix was also inspected at Jericho. Geometry checks verify slope-following stones and channel floors, unchanged horizontal positions, finite geometry, a tapering uneven crest and bounded elevation sampling. Terrain fit, geological form, vertical geometry and map alignment remain illustrative. Live provider coverage, private Drive playback and hardware frame rates are separate from these local checks.

unified_map.walking_control: The yellow Walk figure enters supported source models in the same map canvas; it becomes Exit to restore the previous camera and field of view. terrain_integration.method: The whole model follows a bounded 9 by 9 grid of loaded map elevations, preserving source-plan horizontal relationships. Soil, rock and instanced scree share the same displacement, and long channel floors follow its local slope. The irregular apron and soil-covered ridge back fade into the map. The crest is uneven and the rock ends taper, replacing the rectangular tile and full-depth slabs. All vertical deformation, terrain fitting and geological scenery are illustrative, not survey registration.
terrain_integration.elevation_loading: Retain last loaded nonzero elevation samples during missing-coverage zero responses, separately from vertical exaggeration. Keep the close-up scale when entering Terrain, and synchronize the camera with loaded elevation while preserving independent eye-level movement.
terrain_integration.regression_fixture: atlas/scripts/fixtures/negative-terrain.png: original constant Terrarium DEM at -183 metres, for a controlled below-sea-level camera and model test; no source-image pixels.
terrain_integration.transparency: Feathered ground and ridge skirts do not write depth, and draw before cliff faces; fully invisible pixels cannot hide ground behind them. The shared landscape ground uses the same rule.

unified_map.character_validation: Deterministic physics checks pass for sprinting against a thin wall, wall sliding, low steps, tall ledges, jumping/gravity, ceiling head clearance, crouching, transformed masonry instances, climbable slopes and steep-cliff rejection. The actual Qumran model stops a sprint at its tunnel masonry before and after a sloped terrain fit, without lifting the body onto the cliff crest. Input checks cover double-tap S and W, key repeat, release and blur. Final desktop and phone Chromium checks on actual Pages output (88.8 MiB) held movement against the real masonry over successive rendered frames, jumped and landed under gravity, crouched and entered sprint through keyboard/phone controls. Desktop blur clears held movement and the phone Sprint toggle gives immediate selected-state feedback. The map canvas survives the complete flow and returning overhead. The embodied view and return also render correctly on the existing archived Wadi Qumran Mapterhorn patch; the desktop render was visually inspected.
